body.text:
In your implementation of the substance-gate, when an adjudicator reviews a dialogue and returns `needs_revision`, the cycle router correctly routes back to the target job (attempt is bumped, and verdicts/blockers are reset). However, during the next cycle (attempt 2), the adjudicator runs again and tries to publish a new `collaboration_ledger` artifact with the same logical name `collaboration_ledger` but modified content (new entries, new verdict, or new rationale).

Since `publishArtifact` in `go/pkg/mutations/artifact.go` enforces that `existing` artifacts with the same logical name and job ID must match the content hash (otherwise returning `artifact logical name already exists with different content`), and since `resetJobToBlocked` does NOT delete existing rows from `striatumd.artifacts`, how can a subsequent cycle iteration ever successfully publish its new ledger without failing on the content hash mismatch? Was the `cycle_<N>` unique path/logical name naming convention described in the design synthesis actually implemented to prevent this?

No. In the code I landed, the cycle_<N> unique path/logical-name convention was not implemented. The generated adjudicator job still has static logical_name collaboration_ledger and a static COLLABORATION_LEDGER.md path, and resetJobToBlocked does not remove prior artifacts or create attempt-scoped artifact slots. Therefore an attempt-2 adjudicator publishing modified ledger content for the same job_id/logical_name would hit publishArtifact content-hash mismatch and fail, unless it republished byte-identical content. This is a real V1 bug and the design-synthesis convention is not satisfied. The follow-up fix should make collaboration-ledger publication attempt-scoped, either by giving artifact rows/job expected artifacts an attempt dimension, or by dynamically generating cycle_<attempt> logical names and paths in the work packet and expected-artifact checks. Deleting old artifact rows would be the weaker option because it loses durable provenance.
